200.description:
OK

Identity validation has been successfully initiated. In the response, **otp.status** will be set to **Offered** if One-Time Passcode  Authentication should be used. To use OTP, first call [Generate OTP](generateotp) to request that a one-time passcode  be sent to the consumer's phone. Then, have the consumer enter the code in your application and call [Verify OTP](verifyotppasscode)  to validate the code entered matches the code sent. If Knowledge-Based Verification is to be used, **kba.status** will be set to **Offered**  and out-of-wallet questions along with possible answers will be included in the response. These questions and possible answers should be  presented to the consumer and their answers validated using [Validate KBA](validatekba).

IdverifyKBAResponse.description: Represents the response to the Knowledge-Based Authentication API.

jwtToken.description: Upon successful validation of the consumer's identity (i.e., kba.status = "Passed"), a new JSON Web Token will be returned.  This new bearer token should be passed in the Authorization header for all subsequent API calls.

IdverifyKBAStatus.description:
Represents the status of the Knowledge-Based Verification. The status may be:

```  
Ineligible*:    KBA cannot be used to confirm the consumer's identity.
Offered*^:      Knowledge-based verification questions are included in the response. Call Validate KBA API with the consumer's answers to these questions to validate the consumer's identity.
Passed^:        The answers provided matched and the consumer's identity validated.
Failed^:        The answers provided did not match and the consumer's identity could not be validated.
Error*^:        An unexpected error has occurred.
Abandoned^:     Answers not supplied; verification has been abandoned
```

\* Possible status returned from [Validate Identity](validateidentity)
^  Possible status returned from [Validate KBA](validatekba)

IdverifyOTP.description: Represents the One-Time Passcode Authentication status.

IdverifyOTPResponse.description: Represents the response to the One-Time Passcode Authentication API.

jwtToken.description: Upon successful validation of the consumer's identity (i.e., otp.status = "Passed"), a new JSON Web Token will be returned.  This new bearer token should be passed in the Authorization header for all subsequent API calls.

IdverifyOTPStatus.description:
Represents the status of the One-Time Passcode Authentication. The status may be:

```  
Ineligible*:    OTP cannot be used to confirm the consumer's identity.
Offered*:       OTP can be used for identity validation. Call Generate OTP API to request that a one-time passcode be sent to the consumer's phone.
In Progress^:   OTP passcode has been sent to the consumer's phone.
Passed':        The passcode matched the passcode sent to the consumer's phone and the consumer's identity has been validated.
Failed':        The passcode did not match the passcode sent to the consumer's phone. You may allow the consumer to re-enter the code and try again.
Max Retry Hit': The maximum number of attempts to validate the passcode has been reached and the consumer's identity cannot be validated.
Error*^':        An unexpected error has occurred.
```

\* Possible status returned from [Validate Identity](validateidentity)
^  Possible status returned from [Generate OTP](generateotp)
\' Possible status returned from [Verify OTP](verifyotppasscode)

IdverifySessionType.description:
Indicates the type of session being used.

**0** should be used for non-digital cases and digital cases where JavaScript is used to collect device information. (Default)
**1** should be used for digital cases where the device information was captured from a mobile SDK.
